reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that team-level aggregates provide superior predictive power compared to individual lineup features in soccer score prediction. This is due to reduced noise and higher signal-to-noise ratio in aggregated data. The method employs two independent regression models for home and away goals, which are then combined into a scoreline. The evaluation protocol includes fitness metrics (MAE, RMSE, R2), real-world performance (Kendall tau, top-4/relegation accuracy), and a betting simulation with fixed-stake £1 wagers. The failure mode occurs when individual player features become over-granular and introduce spurious correlations. The betting simulation lacks a proper odds baseline, limiting its ability to validate true edge. The structural findings—goalkeeper dominance and aggregate superiority—are transferable across sports despite differing scoring dynamics.
